implementation_notes: Ktor's routing DSL is a direct ADR realization: get("/users/{id}") { ... } installs a handler for that method and path (the Action), the handler reads call.parameters or call.receive, and the Responder role is call.respond(value) / call.respondText(...) with the ContentNegotiation plugin choosing the serialization. Ktor permits multiple matching route handlers, so one-handler-per-request is a design convention enforced by route organization and ordering, not by the router. Keep the domain in a plain class injected into the handler. The classic responder object is justified when one action must answer HTML and JSON, where a small mapper function per format replaces the inline respond call.
pitfalls: call.respond may be invoked only once per request: a second call fails at runtime, so branch with return@get instead of falling through.
Blocking JDBC or file calls inside a coroutine handler block the event loop; wrap them in withContext(Dispatchers.IO).
Without the ContentNegotiation plugin, call.respond on an object throws instead of serializing it.
